reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every finite subset S of N={0,1,2,...}, every coefficient sequence c:N -> R, and every pair w,z in E satisfying ||w||=1 and ||z||=1, define F_(S,c)(v)=sum_(j in S) c(j) Phi_j(v) for v in E. Then the real Hilbert-space inner product satisfies <F_(S,c)(w),F_(S,c)(z)>_(L^2(gamma_E;R)) = sum_(j in S) j! c(j)^2 <w,z>^j. The factorial is interpreted as a real number. The same finite set and same real coefficients occur in both features. Equivalently, the left side is the Gaussian integral of the product of the two displayed finite Hermite sums. This is an exact scalar equality for all such unit w,z, including an empty S and indices j=0.
objects: The finite L^2 feature F_(S,c), its Hilbert-space inner product at w,z, and the finite polynomial in <w,z>.
domains: S finite subset of N; c any N -> R; w,z unit vectors of E; equality in R.
quantifiers: For every admissible E, every S and c, and every w,z with ||w||=||z||=1, the stated identity holds.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product structure with Borel sigma-algebra; S finite; both w and z have norm one. No coefficient sign, support, or normalization condition is imposed.
scopes: Exact real-valued inner-product identity on pairs of unit parameters; the feature itself is defined on all E. No probabilistic high-probability or almost-everywhere restriction on w,z occurs.
constant_dependencies: The identity depends on E,S,c,w,z. Each weight is the fixed quantity j! c(j)^2; no unspecified multiplicative or error constant occurs. Values of c outside S are irrelevant.
semantic_notes: Both norm-one assumptions are explicit and must be retained.
The coefficients are squared because the same feature coefficients are used in both arguments.
The Hermite normalization is unnormalized probabilists, accounting for the factorial.
For j=0 the natural-number power has value 1, including when <w,z>=0.
